SEE WHAT THE WHEEL WILL NEED.

Beyond a single height.

Follow a finite-width wheel corridor across soil and rock. Inspect the source tiles, buried layers and vertical faces delivered before each prescribed movement.

Request experiment

SYNTHETIC

2 cm sample cells, 60 mm tyre width, 20 mm margin. Prescribed positions and heading interpolate linearly over each 50 ms interval. No tyre forces or soil deformation are calculated.

Layers and explicit rock faces

Brown: soil. Orange: rock. Arrows are outward geometric face normals, not forces. The cutaway shows the authored source; cyan ticks identify columns delivered in the selected request. Unknown depth below −0.20 m is not filled with assumed bedrock.

What this establishes

Geometry delivery across finite width, continuous swept coverage, layered samples and explicit rock faces. Missing required data holds movement. This experiment does not establish tyre contact pressure, slip, soil stiffness, component survival or real-time performance.

Later experiments must receive distributed tyre deformation, mud and root layers, shared front/rear history, rim/spoke/bead failure and 3D lateral/turning forces. Source values here are authored examples, not scanned or calibrated trail data.
